claim.quote: Here we report the observation of the 1S–2S transition in magnetically trapped atoms of antihydrogen.

date.note: Nature online publication date (19 December 2016); the print issue is 26 January 2017.

key_value_text.quote: Our result is consistent with CPT invariance at a relative precision of about 2 × 10−10.
key_value_text.value: 1S–2S frequency consistent with hydrogen; CPT test at a relative precision of about 2 × 10−10

name: Observation of the 1S–2S transition in trapped antihydrogen

significance.quote: Our result is consistent with CPT invariance at a relative precision of about 2 × 10−10.
significance.value: Consistent with CPT invariance at a relative precision of about 2 × 10−10 (no sigma level stated)

summary.plain: ALPHA used a laser to excite the 1S to 2S transition in trapped antihydrogen and found its frequency consistent with that of hydrogen. The paper calls it the most precise measurement performed on an anti-atom.
summary.technical: Two-photon (243 nm) 1S–2S excitation of magnetically trapped antihydrogen; the transition frequency is consistent with that expected for hydrogen in the same environment, consistent with CPT invariance at a relative precision of about 2 x 10^-10.

title: Observation of the 1S–2S transition in trapped antihydrogen
why_it_matters: The abstract says the CPT theorem requires hydrogen and antihydrogen to have the same spectrum, so any difference would signal CPT violation.
